headline: ASX climbs as WiseTech jumps, while gold and oil rebound
paragraphs: Australian shares rose for a second day. The ASX 200 closed Friday up 69.8 points, or 0.8%, at 8,833.60. Technology helped lead the gains: WiseTech jumped 14.5% after the logistics software group reaffirmed its annual revenue outlook and said CargoWise revenue had grown 11% in the four months to October. Miners and gold stocks also helped lift the index.

The local rally came without a fresh lead from Wall Street, which was shut Thursday for Thanksgiving. Wednesday remains the latest US cash session: the S&P 500 fell 0.25% to 7,182.78 and the Nasdaq-100 fell 0.64% to 26,046.90, while the Dow gained 0.33%. The next test for US tech comes in Friday’s shortened New York session, which runs from 1:30 am to 5 am Saturday Sydney time.

The Australian dollar rose to 66.64 US cents at 4:09 pm Sydney, up 0.44% against MarketWatch’s previous reference. Gold also rebounded: Kitco’s spot bid reached US$3,651 a troy ounce at 5:46 pm, up 2.4% against its reference. Reuters described the move as a bounce from Wednesday’s one-year low as the sell-off in AI-linked shares eased, even as US rate-rise expectations remained a headwind.

January Brent was quoted at US$97.27 a barrel at 5:46 pm Sydney, up 0.72% from Thursday’s US$96.57 settlement. That was a delayed Friday quote, not a settlement. Reuters pointed to concerns about shipments through the Strait of Hormuz and attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure, a separate driver from the rebound in tech shares.
